title: Expected Fixed Points of a Random Permutation (OQ-02-OQ-02)
description: Formal proof that the total number of fixed points across all permutations of n elements equals n!, equivalently E[#fixed points] = 1, via Burnside's lemma. Also proves the weighted partition identity ∑_k k·C(n,k)·D(n-k) = n! by double counting.

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: Proof of ∑_σ |Fix(σ)| = n! via Burnside's lemma using MulAction.sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group
Proof that exactly (n-1)! permutations fix any given point via orbit-stabilizer theorem
Proof of the weighted partition identity ∑_k k·C(n,k)·D(n-k) = n! by double counting with Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
Connection between Burnside's lemma, the orbit-stabilizer theorem, and the derangement formula S(n,k) = C(n,k)·D(n-k)

overview.historicalContext: The expected number of fixed points of a uniformly random permutation equals 1, for any n ≥ 1. This follows elegantly from linearity of expectation: each of the n positions i is fixed (i.e., σ(i) = i) with probability 1/n, giving total expectation n·(1/n) = 1. The formal version — that the sum ∑_σ |Fix(σ)| = n! — was understood implicitly by combinatorialists through the 19th century. The modern group-theoretic perspective comes from Burnside's 1897 'Theory of Groups of Finite Order', where the orbit-counting lemma (Burnside's lemma, sometimes attributed to Cauchy and Frobenius) establishes ∑_g |Fix(g)| = |orbits| · |G|. For the symmetric group S_n acting on {1,…,n}, transitivity reduces this to n! immediately. The derangement connection — expressing the fixed-point distribution as S(n,k) = C(n,k)·D(n-k) — links to the 18th century 'problème des rencontres' (Montmort 1708, de Moivre 1718), and the weighted partition identity ∑_k k·S(n,k) = n! is the first-moment formula for this distribution. In modern probability, this is the canonical example showing that the number of fixed points converges in distribution to Poisson(1) as n → ∞ (Chen-Stein method), with mean and variance both equal to 1 in the limit.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that ∑_{σ ∈ Perm(Fin n)} |Fix(σ)| = n! for n ≥ 1, and prove the weighted partition identity ∑_k k·C(n,k)·D(n-k) = n! arising from the partial derangement formula S(n,k) = C(n,k)·D(n-k).
overview.proofStrategy: For the main theorem (`sum_fixedPoints_eq_factorial`): Burnside's lemma in the form `MulAction.sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group` gives ∑_σ |Fix(σ)| = |orbits| · |G|. The action of Perm(Fin n) on Fin n is pretransitive (Equiv.swap x y sends x to y for any y), so the orbit quotient type is `Unique` — it has exactly one element. Thus |orbits| = 1 and |G| = n!. For `card_perm_fixing_point`: the orbit-stabilizer theorem (`MulAction.orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer` and `Subgroup.card_mul_index`) gives n · |Stab(x)| = n!, so |Stab(x)| = (n-1)!. For the weighted identity (`weighted_partition_identity`): double counting with `Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to` swaps the summation order, converting ∑_k k·|A_k| (where A_k = {σ : fp(σ) = k}) to ∑_σ fp(σ) = n!.
keyInsights: Burnside's lemma (MulAction.sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group) directly gives the sum without needing to compute individual fixed-point sets
Transitivity of Perm(Fin n) on Fin n collapses the orbit count to 1: the orbit quotient type `orbitRel.Quotient` is provably `Unique` via `pretransitive_iff_unique_quotient_of_nonempty`
The orbit-stabilizer theorem yields `card_perm_fixing_point`: exactly (n-1)! permutations fix any given element x, because the stabilizer of x in Perm(Fin n) is isomorphic to Perm(Fin (n-1))
Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to is the key double-counting lemma: it rigorously swaps ∑_k ∑_{σ ∈ A_k} f(σ) = ∑_σ f(σ) without any sorry
The `native_decide` tactic provides computational verification for small cases (n=1,2,3,4), giving checkable evidence before the general proof
prerequisites: Partial derangement counts from parent DerangementsOQ02

sections.title: Header, Imports, and Module Setup
sections.description: Module docstring stating both main results (sum_fixedPoints_eq_factorial and weighted_partition_identity), proof strategies for each, and imports from Mathlib's group action and permutation libraries. Opens the DerangementsOQ02OQ02 namespace.

sections.title: Section I: Concrete Verifications
sections.description: Four `native_decide` theorems verifying both identities for n=3 and n=4. For n=3: ∑_σ |Fix(σ)| = 6 = 3! across all 6 permutations; weighted sum breakdown 0+3+0+3=6. For n=4: ∑_σ |Fix(σ)| = 24 = 4!; weighted breakdown 0+8+12+0+4=24. These serve as computational witnesses before the general proof.

sections.title: Section II: Boundary Values
sections.description: Three boundary theorems for n=0,1,2: the empty case (sum=0, since Fin 0 is empty), the trivial case (n=1: only the identity, 1 fixed point, total=1=1!), and n=2 (identity contributes 2, swap contributes 0, total=2=2!). All proved by `native_decide` or `simp`.

sections.title: Section III: Key Lemma via Orbit-Stabilizer
sections.description: Proves `card_perm_fixing_point`: for n ≥ 1, exactly (n-1)! permutations of Fin n fix any given point x. The six-step proof: (1) identify {σ | σ x = x} as the stabilizer subgroup via `Equiv.subtypeEquiv`; (2) show the orbit of x is all of Fin n using `Equiv.swap x y`; (3) compute |orbit(x)| = n; (4) apply orbit-stabilizer theorem via `orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer` and `Subgroup.card_mul_index`; (5) compute |G| = n!; (6) cancel n to get |Stab| = (n-1)!.

sections.title: Section IV: Main Theorem via Burnside's Lemma
sections.description: Proves `sum_fixedPoints_eq_factorial` for n ≥ 1: the private helper `filter_eq_fixedBy_card` rewrites the filter card as `Fintype.card (MulAction.fixedBy (Fin n) σ)`. Then `MulAction.sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group` applies Burnside's lemma. Transitivity is witnessed by `pretransitive_iff_unique_quotient_of_nonempty`, making the orbit quotient `Unique` (card 1). The result follows: 1 · n! = n!.

sections.title: Section V: Weighted Partition Identity
sections.description: Proves `weighted_partition_identity`: ∑_{k=0}^n k·C(n,k)·D(n-k) = n! and `total_fixed_eq_card_perm`. The double-counting argument in two steps: Step 1 uses `card_perms_with_kfixed` (from parent file) to convert k·C(n,k)·D(n-k) into a sum over the fiber A_k = {σ : fp(σ)=k}. Step 2 applies `Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to` to swap the summation, yielding ∑_σ fp(σ) = n!. Uses `set_option maxHeartbeats 800000` for the elaboration-heavy proof.

sections.title: Section VI: Summary and Generating Function Interpretation
sections.description: The theorem `summary_expected_fixed_one` packages the two identities together: given ∑_k C(n,k)·D(n-k) = n! (from the parent derangements-oq-02 file), both the unweighted and weighted sums equal n!. The docstring interprets this as: the bivariate generating function G_n(t) = ∑_k S(n,k)·t^k satisfies G_n(1) = G_n'(1) = n!, meaning E[1] = E[#fixed] = 1.

conclusion.summary: This file proves 13 theorems (including concrete verifications for n=1,2,3,4) with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, establishing both the Burnside-based main theorem and the weighted partition identity by double counting.
conclusion.implications: The result confirms E[#fixed] = 1 in Lean and provides a rigorous connection between the derangement formula S(n,k) = C(n,k)·D(n-k) and moment calculations. The `card_perm_fixing_point` lemma (orbit-stabilizer) is a reusable result for permutation group theory. The proof technique — Burnside's lemma combined with transitivity of the symmetric group — is a prototype for computing fixed-point sums in any transitive group action.
openQuestions: Prove higher moment formulas: E[(#fixed)^k] for k ≥ 2 (second moment E[(#fixed)^2] = 2 for n ≥ 2)
